transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jesse Lin (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Ortiz (Sunrise Head of Data), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Sara Blake (Compliance)

Summary (auto):
Sunrise Health is evaluating Redwood for a 6-week POC to validate inference quality and secure data handling for a patient-facing triage assistant. Key concerns: PHI handling, log retention and redaction, ability to disable or minimize prompt storage, and deployment options (hosted w/ BAA vs Private VPC/on-prem). Customer provided rough workload sizing and expects a benchmark run to validate latency and cost.

Topics:
- PII/PHI redaction and logging options
- Retention settings and legal constraints (BAA/HIPAA)
- Prompt storage and ability to opt-out or hash/store only metadata
- Workload sizing for POC: throughput, tokens/request, concurrency
- Success criteria and benchmark plan
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have an hour, we'll try to cover scope for the POC and specifically data handling questions up front.
[00:12] Dr. Maya: Thanks Samir, yeah we, uh, our primary blocker is PHI and retention. We need to know if Redwood will persist prompts that contain patient names and notes. We need to avoid storing raw prompts, or at least redacting them.
[00:28] Jesse: Right, so we have a couple of options. On hosted we can enable prompt redaction at ingest, and we can also enable prompt non-persistence for POC accounts - basically no prompt bodies are written to long-term logs, only metadata. For production we typically recommend Private (VPC) + KMS so customers keep logs in their account.
[00:46] Liam: Can you clarify non-persistence? Does that mean you never see the prompt on Redwood side?
[00:52] Jesse: Practically, during request processing ephemeral memory is used - we do see the text in the runtime for inference, but it's not written to audit logs if you opt-out. There are transient logs for debugging that can be disabled, and we offer configurable retention windows, e.g., 7, 30, 90, 365 days.
[01:08] Sara: For HIPAA we need a BAA and we need to ensure logs containing PHI are redacted or kept only in our encrypted storage. Also audit trails for access.
[01:16] Samir: Absolutely, Redwood supports BAAs for Private deployments, and we can run the POC under a limited hosted BAA while we evaluate. We have SOC2 reports and can share them.
[01:26] Speaker 2: Sorry, Samir can you share the SOC2 link in the chat, and the data flow diagram?
[01:31] Samir: I'll share SOC2 and our architecture diagram after the call.

[01:45] Jesse: On redaction approaches: we can do pre-ingest client-side redaction with customer rules, server-side regex redaction, or a hybrid where we store hashes for traces. For the POC we recommend server-side redaction plus storing only hashes of identifiers so you can map back locally.
[02:05] Dr. Maya: Storing hashes is interesting. We need to make sure hashing is deterministic and keyed so the same patient ID maps consistently for debug but not reversible.
[02:15] Jesse: Yes, we support HMAC-style hashing with customer-provided key in Private deployments; on hosted we can use a Redwood-managed keyed hash but recommend Private for production PHI.

[02:30] Liam: Workload: for the POC we'll run a simulated 100k messages over 2 weeks, spikes up to 200 rps during business hours, average tokens per request ~220 (including system + user). We need p95 latency under 600ms and p99 under 1.2s for the triage path. Cost target is, eh, our finance wants to see cost under $0.0015 per token for baseline.
[02:55] Samir: Good, that's very actionable. For sizing we'll propose two flavors: hosted with dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) and Private VPC. For the hosted dedicated pool we estimate needing 2 x A100-equivalent pooled instances for your 200 rps spike with batching; for Private on-prem we can give guidance on machine types.
[03:15] Jesse: For the benchmark harness we'll ask for a 500-line sample prompt set representative of PHI redaction cases plus a synthetic load generator. We'll run an initial quality eval on 500 examples to check extraction accuracy and hallucination rates; then throughput bench for 100k messages.
[03:32] Dr. Maya: Success criteria: 1) 95%+ entity extraction accuracy on the example set; 2) p95 <= 600ms on triage path; 3) no raw PHI in persisted logs; 4) documented retention policy applied; 5) code-level reproducible benchmark steps.
[03:48] Jesse: We'll capture those as the POC acceptance criteria. We'll also surface failure modes - like if anonymization increases token counts and cost.

[04:05] Sara: On retention: our legal wants 30 days of logs for the POC, but production might require 365 days in encrypted storage, with immediate deletion of raw prompts after 24 hours. Can Redwood enforce per-route retention?
[04:20] Samir: Yes per-route or per-project retention policies can be configured on Redwood Console. For hosted we store the logs in encrypted buckets; retention is configurable and we can set redaction policies per route. For Private you control the storage entirely.
[04:36] Liam: What about prompt storage for function calls and tool output? We rely on those for debugging. If we disable prompt persistence, do we lose observability?
[04:46] Jesse: You can enable a short retention window (e.g., 7 days) for observability, and we can redact sensitive fields inside the prompt while preserving structural content. Also we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns without storing the full prompt.

[05:05] Dr. Maya: Benchmarks: can Redwood run both accuracy and perf? Or do we run locally with your harness?
[05:12] Jesse: We provide the harness and can run on Redwood infra or give you the scripts to run on your infra. For PHI constraints many customers run the accuracy eval locally with the scripts we provide; Redwood runs the throughput benchmark in a dedicated sandbox if you want reproducible numbers.
[05:27] Samir: We'll propose a plan: week 0 prepare sample data and redaction rules; week 1 run accuracy eval with local execution; week 2 run throughput benchmarks with Redwood harness; week 3 analyze results and tune batching/quantization; week 4 final acceptance. Overall 4-6 weeks for POC.

[05:45] Sara: About encryption: we need KMS integration, ideally with our own key. Is that possible in hosted?
[05:52] Jesse: Hosted offers envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some regions for enterprise customers, but for full BYOK integration we recommend Private deployment. We'll list the exact regions where CMK is supported in the doc.

[06:08] Liam: Any pitfalls? For example, tokenization expanding after redaction or anonymization?
[06:12] Jesse: Yes, if you substitute tokens with long placeholders or add metadata it can increase token count. We can give guidance on redaction patterns to minimize token inflation. Also quantization profiles may impact latency and throughput; will share recommended settings.

[06:30] Samir: Competitors question - how are we different versus Anthropic/OpenAI?
[06:35] Jesse: Main differences: production-first runtime, unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private, and configurable data controls with clear observability. We also give model/quantization recommendations to meet cost/latency targets.

[06:50] Dr. Maya: For the POC acceptance we'll need a short doc showing exactly what gets logged, what is redacted, and who can access logs. Also a runbook for reproducing the benchmark.
[07:00] Samir: We'll include that in the POC SOW.

[07:12] Speaker 3: quick question, can we get a sandbox environment with API keys that restrict access to certain endpoints?
[07:18] Jesse: Yes, we can issue scoped API keys plus route-level RBAC. For the POC we'll create a project with scoped keys and a small console view for your compliance team.

[07:34] Dr. Maya: One operational ask: can we have alerts if redaction fails or regexes misfire?
[07:40] Jesse: We can stream detection events to your SIEM or set up webhook alerts. Also we provide sampling of redacted events for audit under retention rules.

[07:55] Samir: Alright to recap next steps - I'll send SOC2, architecture diagram, and draft SOW with pricing for hosted dedicated vs Private. Jesse will share the benchmark harness and tokenizer notes. Sunrise to provide sample dataset and legal retention windows. We'll plan kickoff week of 2027-01-25.

[08:18] Liam: Sounds good. One more: pricing for benchmarks and short-term dedicated capacity - do you have ballpark numbers now?
[08:26] Samir: Ballpark for a 4-week POC on dedicated pool supporting your spike is about $25k-$40k depending on GPU type and ingress. We'll put a detailed line-item in the SOW.

[08:40] Sara: Also note we'll need vendor risk questionnaire filled out before any entitlements.
[08:45] Samir: We'll have someone from Security fill that and return within 3 business days.

[09:00] End recap and scheduling
